solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Second top growth leaves behind a S African succulent

indicators.note: to leave something behind is to go on without it, so the word for top travels on without its letter a

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
the top of a mountain
a boom is a period of rapid growth

explanation.surface: A botanist describes how a South African plant sheds its leaves from the tips as it grows.
explanation.walkthrough: SPEKBOOM is S + PE(A)K + BOOM; 'leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb that drops the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Spekboom is the Afrikaans name of Portulacaria afra, a fleshy shrub native to South Africa, so it is such a plant.

clue.text: Bone-splicing rod to replace cap in place of femur, at the right length but missing cup?

definitions.text: at the right length but missing cup?

indicators.note: replacing a cap means the first letter of a word is swapped out for something else

parts.note: surgeons fix broken bones with a metal pin
the femur is the thigh bone

explanation.surface: A surgeon fits a rod into a broken thigh bone, worrying about its length.
explanation.walkthrough: The T heading THIGH is swapped for PIN. The definition is golf: the 'cup' is the hole on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a shot finishing pin-high has travelled exactly far enough to be level with the flag, though it has not dropped into the hole.

clue.text: Cookware equipment, one way to serve up tea cups?

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment

indicators.note: to cup something is to hold it inside, so the word for tea encloses the turned letters

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: dishes served up are presented, and in a down entry up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a lane is a narrow way

explanation.surface: Kitchen gear: one way to serve tea is in cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchenalia is a jokey collective term for kitchen utensils and pots, so it covers pans and other gear.

clue.text: Twisting short little bit in two ways, one of us threaded fastener

indicators.note: twisting round makes the shortened word read in the opposite direction
short means cut off before the end, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a jot is a tiny amount
one of us taken two ways: the pronoun I, and me

explanation.surface: A twisted strand threaded through a bead holds one of the party's belongings fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In two ways' tells you to read 'one of us' twice, once as I and once as ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An ojime is a Japanese bead slid along the cords of an inro to keep it closed, a sliding cord fastener.

clue.text: An American independent stooge with USA's top elected representative

parts.note: a mug is a dupe or fall guy
W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of USA
a Member of Parliament is an elected representative

explanation.surface: An American politician standing as an independent is dismissed as a stooge alongside the country's chief lawmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugwump was a Republican who bolted the party in 1884, so the word came to mean a politically independent American.

clue.text: Stock bound by a hostile choreographer

indicators.note: something bound by another is tied up inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a hostile one is an enemy
stock in the sense of family or lineage

explanation.surface: Livestock is tied up by an angry enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Michel Fokine was the Russian dancer who created ballets such as The Dying Swan for the Ballets Russes.

clue.text: Triumphed in South Carolina, within branch overworked by old writer

indicators.note: the word for triumphed sits inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: a fork is where a branch splits off

indicators.note: within places the combined letters inside the word for branch

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina
won means triumphed

explanation.surface: A player who won in South Carolina is described as exhausted by a branch-line commute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By old writer' marks the word as Spenser's.
explanation.definitionFit: Forswonck is Spenser's past participle meaning worn out with toil, an archaism used in The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Acacia tree's durable timber with raised finish

indicators.note: in a down entry raising the finish lifts the last letter up to the top

parts.note: oak is a famously hard-wearing wood

explanation.surface: A carpenter praises acacia wood that is tough and has a raised polish.
explanation.definitionFit: The koa is a Hawaiian species of acacia prized for its timber, used for ukuleles and canoes.

clue.text: Café refurbished in Hornsey

indicators.note: a refurbished place has been done up and rearranged, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A café in Hornsey has been done up.
explanation.walkthrough: Hornsey is a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: A noshery is an informal word for an eatery, from nosh meaning food, so it is a café or restaurant.

clue.text: We don't believe drama with unconvincing grand opera piece not specified

definitions.note: the definition is what the plural answer would say of themselves

parts.note: No is a variant spelling of Noh, Japanese classical drama
a thin excuse is unconvincing
G is short for grand, a thousand
an aria is a solo song in an opera
NS is the abbreviation for not specified

explanation.surface: Critics declare they cannot believe a play with a feeble big-opera number of no stated title.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer itself: people with no religious belief would say they do not believe.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothingarians are people holding no particular creed, so collectively they could say they have no faith.

clue.text: Hungry Shakespearean actor wants this sausage coated with pecan

indicators.note: wants here means lacks, so something is missing from the combined words

parts.note: peckish means slightly hungry

indicators.note: a coating is an outer layer, so what is missing sits on the outside and the inside survives

parts.note: Edmund Kean was the great Shakespearean actor of the Regency stage
names the coat: its letters split into PEC at the front and AN at the back

explanation.surface: A famished actor wants a sausage with a nut crust.
explanation.walkthrough: PECKISH KEAN is the answer with PEC on the front and AN on the back: the letters of pecan coating it. Remove them.
explanation.definitionFit: Kishke is a Jewish dish of beef casing stuffed with seasoned filling, a type of sausage.

clue.text: Sacrificing the lead, queen with three of diamonds played, not in a match

indicators.note: cards that have been played are thrown down in a new order
giving up the lead means the opening letter of the following word is lost

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for with
D for diamonds, three times over

explanation.surface: A card player gives up the lead by playing a queen and the three of diamonds and fails to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a card contest, but it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A match can be a marriage, and someone who has not married is unwedded.

clue.text: Tory lord who could become very fit

indicators.note: saying the letters could become something else invites them to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Conservative peer who might turn into a heartthrob.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit is British slang for sexually attractive, and someone very attractive is so desirable that onlookers salivate.

clue.text: Help with cost, holding note as one provides edible nuts

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the phrase for helping with cost encloses the next letters

parts.note: to chip in is to contribute towards a bill
N is short for note
qua is the Latin-derived word meaning in the capacity of

explanation.surface: Someone helping with a bill hands over a banknote as a contribution.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinquapin is a North American chestnut or oak tree that bears small sweet nuts which can be eaten.

clue.text: Freed from spells of constant injury during nude wrestling

indicators.note: during places the earlier letters inside the period of the rearranged word
wrestling bodies get twisted into new positions, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
c is the symbol for the speed of light, a constant
harm means injury

explanation.surface: A wrestler grappling naked suffers repeated bouts of injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spells' suggests periods of time, but it means magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncharmed means not under any enchantment, so someone released from magic charms is in that state.

clue.text: Horny beast caught in historic scene?

indicators.note: something caught in a phrase is trapped inside it, spanning the boundary between two words
the question mark warns that the trapped letters only match the answer when said out loud

parts.note: the letters running from the end of historic into the start of scene

explanation.surface: An antlered animal is captured in a painting of a famous moment.
explanation.walkthrough: A rare hidden homophone: the hidden letters ORIC S are not the answer's spelling but say the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large African and Arabian antelope with long straight horns, so it is a beast bearing horns.

clue.text: Have will affected by contractions in stomach

indicators.note: a contraction shortens a word by dropping letters and putting an apostrophe in their place

parts.note: have contracts to 've, as in I've
will contracts to 'll, as in I'll

explanation.surface: Someone's resolve is shaken by cramps in the belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contractions' looks like stomach cramps but means shortened words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vell is a dialect name for the fourth stomach of a calf, used for making rennet.

clue.text: Book that is about half-forgotten Ibsen play with interior set

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the short phrase for that is reads the other way

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: having an interior means something else sits inside the shortened title
forgetting half of a title means only part of it is kept

parts.note: Ghosts is a play by Henrik Ibsen
a television set

explanation.surface: A theatre book describes a half-remembered Ibsen production with an elaborate interior set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like stage scenery but is a television set. Ghosts is one of Ibsen's best-known plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Eightvo is an old word for octavo, a book size made by folding sheets into eight leaves.

clue.text: Possible sound of typist's beat stopping carbon copy shortage

indicators.note: stopping a gap means plugging it, so the word for beat goes into the abbreviation

parts.note: cc is the abbreviation for carbon copy
to lick an opponent is to beat them
a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: A typist's rhythm halts when carbon paper runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: Clickclack imitates the repeated tapping of keys and typebars, so it is a noise a typing secretary might make.

clue.text: Point raised in mostly overemotional gathering by a Pole?

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the shortened one
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: icky means sickly sentimental

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a cape is a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone makes a point at a soppy party thrown by a Polish guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is the North or South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice pack is floating sea ice crowded together into a mass, as found in polar waters.

clue.text: Fellow wise woman apparently irritating climber

parts.note: co- as a prefix means fellow, as in co-worker
a wise woman is a witch

explanation.surface: A colleague who is a witch is annoyingly ambitious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a social climber; it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowitch, or cowhage, is a tropical vine whose pods bear stinging hairs that make skin itch.

clue.text: Spain's water to supply what's wanted, endless tropical fruit

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter of the verb is dropped

parts.note: agua is Spanish for water
to cater is to provide what people need

explanation.surface: A Spanish vendor provides water and exotic fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Aguacate is the Spanish name for the avocado, a fruit of warm tropical America.

clue.text: Prevent development of surrounding West African people

indicators.note: surrounding means going all round, so the word before encloses the next letter

parts.note: to choke a plant is to stunt its growth
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Aid agencies try to halt the growth of the area around a West African tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West African' looks like one phrase, but only 'African people' defines; 'West' gives W.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chokwe are a Bantu ethnic group of Angola and the Congo, renowned for masks and carving.

clue.text: Having lost Arabic article, cancel wholesale allowance

indicators.note: having lost something means it is no longer there, so those letters come out

parts.note: to call off an event is to cancel it
al is the definite article in Arabic

explanation.surface: A trader cancels a bulk discount after losing a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloff was a small extra weight given by merchants on goods bought in bulk to cover wastage.

clue.text: I can relate rather engaging published following lines in two notes

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the word for rather holds the word for published

parts.note: te and me are both sol-fa notes, me a variant of mi
L for line, doubled

indicators.note: in puts the lines between the two notes

parts.note: a bit means rather or somewhat
a book that is out has been published

explanation.surface: A storyteller notes that a rather gripping new release comes after several lines between notes.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is an older spelling of the sol-fa note usually written MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tell me about it is a sympathetic idiom used to say you share an experience and understand all too well.

clue.text: Bone up incomplete final part in radio series

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are read from the bottom
incomplete means missing its final letter

parts.note: Zulu is the code word for Z, the last in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A student cramming for an exam on an unfinished final episode of a radio drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone up' looks like a phrase meaning study; 'up' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish legend the luz is a small indestructible bone of the spine from which the body will be raised at resurrection.

clue.text: Worried to splice with variable input

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an input is something put in, so the letter goes inside the word for splice

parts.note: to splice is slang for to marry
z is a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about getting married with uncertain contributions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splice' sounds like joining ropes, but in slang 'get spliced' means marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Towze is an old verb meaning to pull about roughly or tousle, so to worry something as a dog does.

clue.text: Cloth covers for head carriage, stipulation Britain backs

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the whole string is read from the end

parts.note: a shay is a light carriage, a chaise
an if is a condition
UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Head-cloths for the carriage are a condition that Britain supports.
explanation.definitionFit: Kufiyahs are the square cotton headdresses worn by Arab men, folded and held by a cord.
